searchText: Any problems with Wednesday? <@364458974906548225> <@456226577798135808> it would fit better I might have a clash on Wednesday if it is 16:00 UTC, I will probably be OK though It would be 16:00 UTC yep Our sessions at Consensus Distributed ends at 16:00 UTC, and I am in the middle of it, so it should be ok <tkstanczak> I think that the stateless client with a witness download and beam sync for the latest 256 blocks or so can run entirely in memory and is just a few steps away. Then we can improve from there. Not sure if that answers your question. (re @GuthL: I understand this. My question (probably ill asked) is assuming I don't verify all the way the state in the back ground, could I keep up with the upcoming state updates?) <GuthL> Thanks! It does partially. Let me rephrase to be sure: Assuming I'm at the tip of the chain, one could store the 256 block in memory, dumped the latest block on the HDD and verifed the upcoming block in memory. Therefore, one could do exploration of the chain (from a certain point) without the hard requirements to run on a SSD (re @tkstanczak: I think that the stateless client with a witness download and beam sync for the latest 256 blocks or so can run entirely in memory and is just a few steps away. Then we can improve from there. Not sure if that answers your question.) <tkstanczak> what is important to clarofy is that witnesses do not allow to explore the chain but only verify the blocks <tkstanczak> *clarify <tkstanczak> for state exploration you need something like beam sync to play supporting role
